facts.content: Patient presents with a dry cough and runny nose for 5 to 6 days.
facts.source_text: CC: Dry cough and runny nose x5–6 days

facts.content: Patient has a dry, continuous cough that is worse at night and disturbs sleep.
facts.source_text: Dry, continuous cough, worse at night; sleep disturbed

facts.content: Patient reports a sore throat from coughing without pain on swallowing.
Patient reports rhinorrhea.
Patient reports subjective fever and chills without measuring temperature.
Patient reports diffuse myalgias in arms and legs.
Patient reports lethargy and weakness.
Patient denies shortness of breath at rest.
Patient denies chest pain.
Patient denies ear pain or ear discharge.
Patient reports appetite is okay.
Patient had transient diarrhea at the onset of illness which has now resolved.
facts.source_text: transient diarrhea at onset now resolved

facts.content: Patient denies nausea and vomiting.
Patient denies urinary symptoms.
Patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient has hypertension.
Patient takes metformin.
Patient takes lisinopril.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father has type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient lives with a well partner.
Patient works as an IT developer.
Patient is an ex-smoker who quit 6 months ago.
Patient drinks wine, 2 to 3 glasses on up to 3 evenings per week.
facts.source_text: etOH: wine 2–3 glasses on up to 3 evenings/wk

facts.content: Clinician assesses an acute viral illness or upper respiratory tract infection based on 5 to 6 days of dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, and myalgias with no shortness of breath or chest pain and resolved initial diarrhea.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute viral illness/URTI: 5–6 d dry cough, rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias; no SOB/CP; initial diarrhea resolved

facts.content: Clinician notes type 2 diabetes mellitus managed with metformin and reported as controlled by the patient.
facts.source_text: 2) T2DM — on metformin; pt reports controlled

facts.content: Clinician notes hypertension managed with lisinopril and reported as controlled by the patient.
facts.source_text: 3) HTN — on lisinopril; pt reports controlled

facts.content: Clinician notes moderate alcohol use and that counseling was given regarding reduction due to hypertension and diabetes.
facts.source_text: 4) EtOH use (moderate) — counseling given re reduction due to HTN/DM

facts.content: For the acute viral illness or URTI, patient is advised rest.
For the acute viral illness or URTI, patient is advised to increase fluid intake.
For the acute viral illness or URTI, patient may take regular paracetamol as needed.
For the acute viral illness or URTI, patient may consider 1 to 2 days off work.
Clinician explains that the expected course of the acute illness is approximately 7 to 10 days.
Patient is advised to return in 2 to 3 days if there is no improvement.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: return in 2–3 d if no improvement

facts.content: Patient is advised to return sooner if breathing worsens or shortness of breath develops.
If the patient is still febrile and the cough is not improving at review, clinician will consider starting chest antibiotics.
facts.source_text: If still febrile and cough not improving at review, consider chest abx

facts.content: Patient is to continue metformin for type 2 diabetes mellitus and have routine follow-up with their usual clinician.
